question: On 11 July 2025, an amendment1 was adopted in the Hellenic Parliament, ordering a threemonth ban on access to asylum for people arriving irregularly from North Africa by boat, stating that such persons would be returned to their country of transit or origin without registration. The Commission is kindly requested to respond to the following numbered questions: 1.

What is the Commission’s assessment of this amendment in relation to Greece’s obligations under Articles 4, 18 and 19 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, the Asylum Procedures Directive (2013/32/EU), the Reception Conditions Directive (2013/33/EU) and the Return Directive (2008/115/EC)?

What is the Commission’s assessment of the argument used by the Greek authorities, stating that the increased number of arrivals presents an ’asymmetrical threat that supersedes the basis of international and EU law on the asylum procedure’ and an ensuing ‘absolute objective incapacity to process asylum applications in due time’?
In the light of the Commission’s position on questions 1 and 2, what action will it take regarding Greece’s obligations under Article 17 of the Treaty on European Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.12.2025) The Commission is aware of the law that was voted by the Greek government on 11 July 2025, which introduced a three-month suspension on the examination of international protection applications for individuals arriving from North Africa and ordered their immediate return.

Throughout the suspension period, the Commission was in close contact with the Greek authorities to address the concerns raised by this suspension and received assurances of the non-renewal of the measure. The Commission is informed that as of 14 October 2025 the measure has been lifted.

The Commission will closely monitor the situation with the Greek authorities to ensure effective access to the procedures for international protection in full compliance with fundamental rights, including the principle of non-refoulement.
